name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs *after* every major design change, not before. This keeps the design loop fast and fluid while still catching accessibility failures early. The trade-off is that we accept occasional last-minute fixes when contrast slips through—but the speed and focus of iteration outweighs the risk.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A live checker after every change risks training us to ignore warnings until the last second—designers will treat it like a nagging pop-up, not a real guardrail. Better: a pre-submission gate that blocks only when contrast drops below WCAG AA, but lets trivial slips slide; that forces discipline without killing momentum. Settle it with a one-week trial: measure how often it blocks versus how many real failures it catches.

name: Facet

name: Pane
text: Pane: A pre-submission gate still trains us to treat contrast as a hurdle, not a habit—designers will delay fixes until the block pops up, then rush to meet the minimum. Better: a live checker that flags contrast *during* the change, but only surfaces the worst offenders in the commit message; that forces real-time discipline without the gate’s friction. Settle it by testing both: measure how often designers ignore warnings versus how often they preemptively fix issues before submission.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Ship a real-time contrast overlay that flags *only* the worst offenders in the canvas during changes, but blocks submission only if contrast drops below WCAG AA.

Result: A live, unignorable guardrail that trains discipline without killing speed—designers fix big failures early, minor slips slide. Owned by Facet.
